title: Ethiopian Lamb Shank Stew
localName: የበግ ቁስ ወጥ — Ye-Beg Qus Wat
community: Ethiopian restaurant kitchens — the lamb shank wat
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Lamb Shank Wat — whole lamb shanks braised in a deeply flavoured berbere-kibbeh sauce for 2 hours until the meat falls off the bone. The restaurant showpiece — a whole lamb shank half-submerged in deep red berbere sauce, served on injera.
longDesc: Lamb shank wat is the restaurant presentation showpiece — a whole lamb shank, its bone standing proud above the sauce, served on a large injera. The shank is braised in the Key Wat sauce until completely tender, absorbing the berbere deeply throughout.
equipment: Large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Brown shanks in kibbeh — 4 minutes per side. Remove.
Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 3 minutes.
Simmer covered 100—120 minutes until falling tender.
chefTips: Brown the shanks first — adds depth.
The shank bone is the presentation element — do not remove it.
Sauce should be thick enough to coat the shank.
commonMistakes: Short cooking — shank must fall off the bone.
cookingScience: See ETH041 for lamb braising science.
sustainabilityTips: Lamb shank is a secondary cut.
servedWith: Served tableside on a large injera for maximum presentation
reheating: Gently — keep shanks submerged in sauce.
culturalNote: Lamb shank wat is the dish that Ethiopian restaurant chefs use to demonstrate their mastery — a single shank on a large injera, surrounded by berbere sauce, is one of the most visually impressive dishes in Ethiopian cuisine.
